p.src: Now Zhou Yu, upon hearing Zhuge Jin's words, conceived a fresh hatred for Kongming and secretly resolved to have him killed. The next day, he mustered all his officers and went in to take leave of Sun Quan. Sun Quan said, “Go on ahead. I shall raise the army and follow shortly.” Zhou Yu took his leave and departed with Cheng Pu and Lu Su at the head of their troops, inviting Kongming to accompany them. Kongming gladly consented. They boarded the ships together, raised sail and mast, and proceeded in stately succession toward Xiakou. When they were some fifty or sixty li from the Three Rivers Estuary, the ships came to anchor in order. Zhou Yu established his central camp there, while camps were pitched along the Western Hills on shore and troops stationed all around. Kongming alone took up quarters in a tiny boat.

p.src: When Zhou Yu had completed his dispositions, he sent someone to invite Kongming to a council. Kongming came to the central command tent, and after they had exchanged courtesies, Zhou Yu said, “Formerly, Cao Cao had few troops and Yuan Shao many, yet Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shao because he adopted Xu You's counsel and first cut off the provisions at Wuchao. Now Cao Cao has eight hundred and thirty thousand troops, while we have only fifty or sixty thousand. How can we withstand him? We too must first cut off Cao Cao's provisions; only then can we defeat him. I have learned that all his army's grain and fodder are stored at Jutie Mountain. You, Master, lived long in the Han River region and know its terrain well. May I trouble you to go with Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Zhao Yun, and the others? I shall also provide a thousand troops, and you can hasten by night to Jutie Mountain and sever Cao Cao's supply route. Each of us serves his own lord; I trust you will not decline.”

p.src: Kongming thought secretly, “Because he could not persuade me to change allegiance, he has devised this scheme to harm me. If I refuse, I shall certainly be mocked. Better to accept and devise another plan.” He therefore agreed with evident pleasure. Zhou Yu was delighted. Kongming took his leave and went out. Lu Su privately asked Zhou Yu, “Why have you sent Kongming to raid the provisions?” Zhou Yu replied, “I wish to kill Kongming, but I fear becoming a laughingstock. So I shall borrow Cao Cao's hand to kill him and thereby remove a future danger.”

p.src: On hearing this, Lu Su went to see Kongming and discover whether he knew of the plot. He found Kongming showing not the slightest sign of distress, but calmly mustering the troops and horses for departure. Unable to bear it, Lu Su sounded him out, saying, “Can you succeed on this expedition, Master?” Kongming laughed. “In naval warfare, fighting on foot, cavalry combat, and chariot warfare, I have mastered every art. Why should I fear that I shall fail? That is unlike you men of the Southland—you and Zhou Yu can each do only one thing.” Lu Su asked, “In what sense can Gongjin and I do only one thing?” Kongming replied, “I have heard the children of the Southlands chant: ‘To ambush roads and guard passes, count on Zijing; for battle on the river, there is Zhou Yu.’ On land, you gentlemen are capable only of ambushing roads and guarding passes; and Zhou Gongjin is fit only for naval warfare—he cannot fight on land.”

p.src: Lu Su reported these words to Zhou Yu. Zhou Yu said angrily, “How dare he mock me as incapable of fighting on land! There is no need for him to go! I shall personally lead ten thousand cavalry to Jutie Mountain and cut Cao Cao's supply route.” Lu Su conveyed this in turn to Kongming. Kongming laughed. “When Gongjin ordered me to cut off the provisions, his true intention was to have Cao Cao kill me. I therefore teased him with a few words, and Gongjin could not endure them. At this hour, when men of ability are needed, I desire only that the Marquis of Wu and Imperial Inspector Liu unite their hearts; then success can be achieved. If each plots to harm the other, the great enterprise is finished. The traitor Cao is full of schemes and has spent his life cutting the supply routes of others. How could he now fail to guard his own with a powerful force? If Gongjin goes, he will surely be captured. For the present, we should first decide the issue in a naval engagement, blunt the northern army's keen edge, and then seek some ingenious plan to defeat it. I hope, Zijing, that you will explain this tactfully to Gongjin.”

p.src: That very night, Lu Su returned to Zhou Yu and related Kongming's words in full. Zhou Yu shook his head and stamped his feet. “This man's insight surpasses mine tenfold. If I do not eliminate him now, he will surely become a scourge to our state!” Lu Su said, “At this hour, when men are needed, I beg you to place the state above all else. Wait until Cao Cao has been defeated; it will not be too late to deal with him then.” Zhou Yu agreed with him.

p.src: Meanwhile, Xuande instructed Liu Qi to defend Jiangxia, while he himself led his officers and troops toward Xiakou. In the distance along the southern bank, banners could be faintly seen and rank upon rank of spears and halberds. He judged that Eastern Wu had already mobilized its forces. He therefore moved all the troops from Jiangxia and encamped at Fankou. Xuande assembled his followers and said, “Since Kongming went to Eastern Wu, no word whatever has come from him. I do not know how matters stand. Who can go and ascertain the truth, then return with a report?” Mi Zhu said, “I am willing to go.”

p.src: Xuande prepared gifts of sheep and wine and sent Mi Zhu to Eastern Wu, ostensibly to reward its army but actually to learn the true situation. Having received his orders, Mi Zhu took a small boat downstream and proceeded directly to the front of Zhou Yu's great camp. The soldiers reported his arrival to Zhou Yu, who summoned him inside. Mi Zhu bowed twice, conveyed Xuande's respectful regards, and presented the wine and gifts. When Zhou Yu had accepted them, he gave a banquet to entertain Mi Zhu. Mi Zhu said, “Kongming has been here a long time. I should now like to return with him.” Zhou Yu replied, “Kongming is presently helping me plan Cao Cao's defeat. How can he leave at once? I too wish to see Liu, Governor of Yuzhou, so that we may discuss a sound strategy together; but as I command the great army, I cannot leave it even briefly. If the Governor of Yuzhou would deign to come here, it would deeply gratify my hopes.”

p.src: Mi Zhu assented, bowed in farewell, and returned. Lu Su asked Zhou Yu, “Why do you wish to see Xuande? What plan do you have?” Zhou Yu replied, “Xuande is a formidable hero of the age and must be eliminated. I shall seize this opportunity to lure him here and kill him, thereby truly removing a future danger to our state.” Lu Su remonstrated with him again and again, but Zhou Yu would not listen. He issued a secret order: “If Xuande comes, first conceal fifty swordsmen and axemen behind the tent hangings. Watch for me to throw down my cup as the signal, then rush out and strike.”

p.src: Meanwhile, Mi Zhu returned to Xuande and reported in detail that Zhou Yu wished to invite his lord to meet him in person and discuss further plans. Xuande at once ordered a swift boat prepared, intending to depart immediately. Guan Yu remonstrated, “Zhou Yu is a man of many schemes, and no letter has come from Kongming. I fear there is deceit in this; you must not go rashly.” Xuande replied, “I have now allied with Eastern Wu so that together we may defeat Cao Cao. Zhou Yu wishes to see me; if I do not go, I shall not be acting in the spirit of an ally. If the two sides distrust one another, nothing can succeed.” Guan Yu said, “If Elder Brother is determined to go, I wish to accompany you.” Zhang Fei said, “I shall go too.” Xuande said, “Only Guan Yu will come with me. Yide and Zhao Yun are to guard the camp, while Jian Yong is to hold E County securely. I shall return as soon as I have gone.”

p.src: When he had given these instructions, Xuande boarded a small boat with Guan Yu and a retinue of more than twenty men, and they sped their oars toward Jiangdong. Xuande observed Eastern Wu's war junks and battleships, its banners, armored troops, and weapons, all arrayed in perfect order on either side, and was greatly pleased. A soldier hurried to report to Zhou Yu, “Liu, Governor of Yuzhou, has arrived.” Zhou Yu asked, “How many ships has he brought?” The soldier answered, “Only one ship, with a retinue of a little over twenty men.” Zhou Yu laughed. “This man's destined hour has come!” He ordered the swordsmen and axemen to take their places in ambush, then went out of the camp to welcome Xuande.

I, Liu Bei, am a man of no ability; why should you honor me with such ceremony?” They therefore sat according to the places of host and guest, and Zhou Yu gave a banquet for Xuande.

p.src: Meanwhile, Kongming happened to come to the riverbank. Hearing that Xuande had come to meet the Commander-in-Chief, he was startled and hurried to the central command tent to observe events in secret. He saw a murderous look on Zhou Yu's face and ranks of swordsmen and axemen hidden behind the hangings on either side. Kongming was greatly alarmed. “What is to be done in such a situation?” He looked back at Xuande, who was talking and laughing with perfect composure; then he noticed a man standing behind Xuande with one hand on his sword—it was Guan Yu. Kongming rejoiced. “My lord is in no danger.” He therefore went no farther inside, but turned back and waited at the riverbank.

p.src: A little while later, Lu Su entered. Xuande asked, “Where is Kongming? May I trouble you, Zijing, to invite him here for a meeting?” Yu said, “It will not be too late to meet Kongming after Cao Cao has been defeated.” Xuande dared say no more. Yun Chang glanced meaningfully at Xuande. Understanding him, Xuande immediately rose and took leave of Yu, saying, “For the present, I, Bei, must bid you farewell. When you have defeated the enemy and won your triumph, I shall come especially to offer my congratulations.” Yu made no effort to detain him and escorted him beyond the camp gate.

p.src: After taking leave of Zhou Yu, Xuande went with Yun Chang and the others to the riverbank, where they found Kongming already aboard a boat. Xuande was overjoyed. Kongming said, “My lord, were you aware of the danger you faced today?” Xuande replied in astonishment, “I was not.” Kongming said, “Had Yun Chang not been there, my lord, you would very nearly have been murdered by Zhou Yu.” Only then did Xuande understand, and he invited Kongming to return with him to Fankou. Kongming said, “Though I, Liang, dwell in the tiger’s jaws, I am as secure as Mount Tai. For now, my lord, simply prepare your vessels, troops, and horses for use. After the twentieth day of the eleventh month, a jiazi day, have Zilong come in a small boat and wait by the southern bank. Be certain there is no mistake.” Xuande asked what he meant. Kongming replied, “Only watch for the southeast wind to rise; then I, Liang, shall surely return.” When Xuande was about to question him further, Kongming urged him to set sail with all speed. Having said this, he returned alone. Xuande, Yun Chang, and their attendants set sail. They had traveled scarcely a few li when suddenly they saw fifty or sixty boats descending from upstream. At the prow of the foremost vessel stood a great general holding his spear crosswise: it was Zhang Fei. Fearing that Xuande might come to harm and that Yun Chang could not manage alone, he had come especially to reinforce them. The three then returned to camp together, and nothing further need be said of it.

p.src: Now Zhou Yu, having seen Xuande off, returned to camp. Lu Su entered and asked, “Since you lured Xuande here, why did you not strike?” Yu replied, “Guan Yun Chang is one of the world’s tiger-like generals. He follows Xuande whether walking or sitting. Had I struck, he would certainly have come to kill me.” Lu Su was dumbfounded. Suddenly it was reported that Cao Cao had sent an envoy bearing a letter, and Yu ordered him admitted. When the envoy presented the letter, the inscription on its cover read: “From the Grand Chancellor of Han, to be opened by Commander-in-Chief Zhou.” Zhou Yu flew into a rage. Without even opening the letter, he tore it to pieces, flung them to the ground, and shouted for the envoy to be beheaded. Lu Su said, “When two states contend, envoys are not put to death.” Yu replied, “I shall execute the envoy as a display of might.” He thereupon had the envoy beheaded and gave the head to an attendant to carry back. He then appointed Gan Ning vanguard, Han Dang commander of the left wing, and Jiang Qin commander of the right, while Yu himself led the other generals in support. The next day they were to prepare their meal at the fourth watch, launch the vessels at the fifth, and advance with drums beating and battle cries ringing.

p.src: Now when Cao Cao learned that Zhou Yu had destroyed his letter and beheaded his envoy, he was furious. He summoned Cai Mao, Zhang Yun, and the other surrendered generals of Jingzhou to form the vanguard. Cao Cao himself commanded the rear army and hurried the warships onward to the mouth of the Three Rivers. They soon saw the vessels of the Eastern Wu advancing so thickly that they covered the river. At their head sat a great general upon the prow, crying loudly, “I am Gan Ning! Who dares come and fight me?” Cai Mao ordered his younger brother Cai Xun to advance. As the two boats drew near, Gan Ning took up his bow, set an arrow to the string, and shot at Cai Xun, who fell at the twang of the bowstring. Gan Ning then drove his vessel swiftly forward. Ten thousand crossbows discharged together, and Cao Cao’s army could not withstand them. Jiang Qin on the right and Han Dang on the left charged straight into Cao Cao’s ranks. Most of Cao Cao’s troops were men of Qingzhou and Xuzhou, long unaccustomed to naval warfare. Out upon the great river, the moment their warships rocked, they could no longer keep their footing. The three squadrons under Gan Ning and the others swept freely back and forth across the water. Zhou Yu pressed more vessels forward to join the battle. The soldiers of Cao Cao’s army struck by arrows and missiles were beyond counting. The fighting continued from the hour of the Snake until the hour of the Goat. Though Zhou Yu had gained the advantage, he feared his smaller force could not withstand the enemy’s numbers, and so ordered the gongs sounded and the vessels recalled.

p.src: Cao Cao’s army returned in defeat. Cao Cao went up to the land camp, reorganized his troops, and summoned Cai Mao and Zhang Yun to rebuke them: “The forces of the Eastern Wu are few, yet we were defeated by them. This is only because you did not apply yourselves!” Cai Mao said, “The Jingzhou navy has gone long without drilling; and the troops of Qingzhou and Xuzhou have never been accustomed to naval warfare. That is why we suffered defeat. We must first establish a naval stockade, placing the Qingzhou and Xuzhou troops within and the Jingzhou troops without, then drill them daily until they are thoroughly proficient. Only then can they be employed.” Cao Cao said, “Since you are commanders of the navy, you may act as circumstances require. Why must you report everything to me?” Thereupon Zhang Yun and Cai Mao went off to train the navy themselves. Along the river they divided the camp into twenty-four water gates. Large vessels stood outside like city walls, while smaller craft lay within and could pass freely to and fro. When evening came, lamps and fires were lit, making the center of the sky and the surface of the water glow crimson. The land camp stretched for more than three hundred li, with its fires unbroken from end to end.

u.src: Cao Cao’s army returned in defeat. Cao Cao went up to the land camp, reorganized his troops, and summoned Cai Mao and Zhang Yun to rebuke them: “The forces of the Eastern Wu are few, yet we were defeated by them. This is only because you did not apply yourselves!”
Cai Mao said, “The Jingzhou navy has gone long without drilling;
and the troops of Qingzhou and Xuzhou have never been accustomed to naval warfare. That is why we suffered defeat.

We must first establish a naval stockade, placing the Qingzhou and Xuzhou troops within and the Jingzhou troops without, then drill them daily until they are thoroughly proficient. Only then can they be employed.”

p.src: Now Zhou Yu returned victorious to camp and rewarded the whole army, while also sending a man to report the victory to the Marquis of Wu. That night, Yu climbed to a high place and looked out. He saw firelight in the west reaching to the heavens. His attendants told him, “That is all the light from the Northern Army’s lamps and fires.” Yu too was alarmed at heart. The next day, wishing to inspect Cao Cao’s naval stockade in person, Yu had a tower ship prepared. Taking musicians and several stalwart generals, each armed with a powerful bow and stout crossbow, he boarded with them and proceeded slowly onward. On reaching the edge of Cao Cao’s camp, Yu ordered the anchor stone dropped, and all the drums and music aboard the tower ship began to play. Secretly observing the naval stockade, Yu exclaimed in great alarm, “This arrangement has truly mastered the essentials of naval warfare!” He asked, “Who commands the navy?” His attendants replied, “Cai Mao and Zhang Yun.” Yu thought, “Those two have long lived east of the river and are thoroughly versed in naval warfare. I must devise a scheme to eliminate them first; only then can Cao Cao be defeated.”

p.src: While he was still observing, a swift report had already reached Cao Cao’s army: “Zhou Yu is spying upon our camp.” Cao Cao ordered vessels launched to capture him. Seeing the signal flags move within the naval stockade, Yu hastily ordered the anchor stone raised. On every side the oarsmen turned their sweeps and paddles together, and the vessel sped away across the river as if in flight. By the time vessels emerged from Cao Cao’s camp, Zhou Yu’s tower ship was already more than ten li away. Unable to catch it, the pursuers returned and reported to Cao Cao.

p.src: Cao Cao asked his generals, “Yesterday’s defeat blunted the edge of our valor; and today he has made a thorough inspection of our camp. What plan should I use to defeat him?” Before he had finished speaking, a man stepped out from below the command tent and said, “From childhood I was a schoolmate and close friend of Zhou Yu. Allow me to rely upon this ever-ready tongue of mine, go to Jiangdong, and persuade him to surrender.” Cao Cao was delighted. Looking at the man, he saw that it was Jiang Gan of Jiujiang, styled Ziyi, who was then serving as a retainer in his command tent. Cao Cao asked, “Ziyi, are you on intimate terms with Zhou Gongjin?” Jiang Gan replied, “Set your mind at ease, Chancellor. When I reach the lands east of the river, I shall certainly succeed.” Cao Cao asked, “What will you need to take with you?” Jiang Gan replied, “I need only one boy to accompany me and two servants to handle the boat. Nothing else is required.” Cao Cao was greatly pleased and gave a farewell banquet for Jiang Gan. Wearing a hempen kerchief and a plain cloth robe, Jiang Gan boarded a small boat and went straight to Zhou Yu’s camp, where he ordered his arrival announced: “Your old friend Jiang Gan has come to visit.” Zhou Yu was discussing affairs in his tent. Hearing that Jiang Gan had arrived, he smiled and said to his generals, “The persuader has come!” He then whispered into the generals’ ears, instructing them what to do. They all accepted their orders and departed.

p.src: Zhou Yu straightened his robes and headdress and came forth with several hundred attendants, all clad in brocade garments and ornate caps, clustered before and behind him. Jiang Gan approached proudly with a young servant in plain blue, and Zhou Yu bowed in welcome. Jiang Gan said, “Gongjin, I trust you have been well since we parted!” Zhou Yu replied, “Ziyi, you have taken great pains. Have you crossed rivers and lakes from afar to act as an envoy for the Cao clan?” Jiang Gan said in astonishment, “Having long been parted from you, I came especially to renew our old friendship. Why do you suspect me of being an envoy?” Zhou Yu laughed. “Though my ear is not as keen as Music Master Kuang’s, I can hear the elegant intent behind the music.” Jiang Gan said, “If this is how you receive an old friend, then allow me to take my leave.” Laughing, Zhou Yu caught him by the arm. “I merely feared that you had come as an envoy for the Cao clan. Since you harbor no such purpose, why leave so hastily?” Thereupon they entered the tent together. When the formal greetings were over and they had taken their seats, Zhou Yu immediately ordered every hero of the region east of the Yangtze summoned to meet Ziyi.

p.src: Before long, the civil officials and military commanders arrived, each dressed in brocade; the subordinate generals and officers under his command all wore silver armor and entered in two files. Zhou Yu had them all exchange greetings, then seat themselves in ranks on either side. He laid out a magnificent banquet, ordered the army’s music of victory played, and had wine served in turn. Zhou Yu told the assembled officers, “This man is my close friend from our school days. Though he has come here from north of the river, he is not an envoy of the Cao household. You gentlemen need have no suspicions.” He then removed his sword and handed it to Taishi Ci, saying, “Wear my sword and act as marshal of the wine. At today’s feast we shall speak only of the affection between friends; whoever mentions Cao Cao or the military affairs of Eastern Wu shall be beheaded at once!”

p.src: Taishi Ci acknowledged the order and sat at the feast with his hand on the sword. Jiang Gan was alarmed and dared say little. Zhou Yu said, “Since taking command of the army, I have not drunk a single drop of wine; but today, having met an old friend and being free of all suspicion, I shall drink until I am drunk.” With that, he laughed heartily and drank freely, while cups and tallies passed busily around the table. When they were half drunk, Zhou Yu took Jiang Gan by the hand and walked with him outside the tent. The soldiers on either side stood fully armed and accoutred, holding spears and halberds. Zhou Yu asked, “Are my soldiers not a fine and mighty sight?” Jiang Gan replied, “They are truly warriors fierce as bears and tigers.”

p.src: Zhou Yu then led Jiang Gan behind the tent for a look; provisions and fodder were piled as high as mountains. Zhou Yu asked, “Are my stores of provisions not amply sufficient?” Jiang Gan replied, “Elite troops and abundant provisions—your reputation is no empty one.” Pretending drunkenness, Zhou Yu laughed loudly and said, “When Zhou Yu and Ziyi studied together, I never dreamed I would see a day like this.” Jiang Gan said, “Given your great talents, brother, this is no more than you deserve.” Taking Jiang Gan’s hand, Zhou Yu said, “When a true man lives in the world and finds a lord who understands him, outwardly they are bound by the duty of sovereign and minister, inwardly by affection as deep as flesh and bone. His words are always acted upon, his plans always followed, and they share fortune and calamity alike. Even if Su Qin, Zhang Yi, Lu Jia, and Master Li were to return to life, with eloquence pouring like a torrent and tongues sharp as blades, how could they ever sway my heart?” Having said this, he burst into laughter. Jiang Gan’s face turned ashen. Zhou Yu again led Jiang Gan into the tent and rejoined the generals in drinking. Pointing to them, he said, “These are all heroes of Jiangdong. Today’s gathering may well be called the ‘Assembly of Heroes.’” They drank until nightfall. When lamps and candles had been lit, Zhou Yu rose, danced with his sword, and sang. His song went: “A man in this world must win merit and fame; merit and fame shall fulfill his life. With my life fulfilled, I shall drink deep; and drinking deep, give voice to a wild song!”

p.src: When the song ended, everyone at the feast laughed with delight. Late in the night, Jiang Gan excused himself, saying, “I can bear no more wine.” Zhou Yu ordered the feast cleared away, and the generals took their leave. Zhou Yu said, “Ziyi and I have not shared a couch for many years. Tonight let us sleep foot to foot.” Then, feigning extreme drunkenness, he led Jiang Gan into the tent to sleep together. Zhou Yu collapsed fully clothed and vomited all around him. How could Jiang Gan possibly fall asleep? As he lay with his head on the pillow listening, the watch drum in the camp sounded the second watch. He rose and saw that the dying lamp still burned. Looking at Zhou Yu, he found him snoring like thunder. Jiang Gan noticed a roll of documents piled on a table inside the tent. He rose from bed and secretly examined them; they were all letters exchanged with others. Among them was one envelope inscribed, “Respectfully sealed by Cai Mao and Zhang Yun.” Jiang Gan was greatly startled and read it in secret. The letter said in essence: “We surrendered to Cao Cao not from any desire for office or emolument, but because circumstances compelled us. We have now lured the northern army into confinement within its camp. As soon as an opportunity presents itself, we shall take the bandit Cao’s head and offer it beneath your command. Sooner or later our messenger will arrive, bringing a report. We beg you not to doubt us. We respectfully send this preliminary reply.”

p.src: Jiang Gan thought, “So Cai Mao and Zhang Yun are secretly allied with Eastern Wu!” He promptly hid the letter inside his clothes. Just as he was about to inspect the other letters, Zhou Yu turned over on the bed. Jiang Gan hurriedly put out the lamp and lay down. Zhou Yu mumbled indistinctly, “Ziyi, within a few days I shall show you the bandit Cao’s head!” Jiang Gan forced himself to answer. Zhou Yu said again, “Ziyi, stay a while! I shall show you the bandit Cao’s head!” But when Jiang Gan questioned him, Zhou Yu had already fallen asleep again.

p.src: Jiang Gan lay on the bed until nearly the fourth watch, when he heard someone enter the tent and call, “Is the Commander-in-Chief awake?” Zhou Yu pretended to start awake from a dream and deliberately asked the man, “Who is sleeping on the bed?” The man replied, “You invited Ziyi to share your bed, Commander-in-Chief. Why have you forgotten?” Zhou Yu said regretfully, “Ordinarily I never drink myself drunk. Yesterday I lost control after becoming drunk. I wonder whether I said anything?” The man said, “Someone has come from north of the river.” Zhou Yu barked, “Keep your voice down!” Then he called, “Ziyi.” Jiang Gan merely pretended to be asleep. Zhou Yu slipped out of the tent. Jiang Gan listened secretly and heard someone outside say, “Commanders Zhang and Cai report: ‘There is no chance to act at once.’” What followed was spoken in so low a voice that he could not hear it clearly.

p.src: A short while later, Zhou Yu returned to the tent and called again, “Ziyi.” Jiang Gan made no answer, but covered his head and feigned sleep. Zhou Yu also undressed and went to bed. Jiang Gan thought, “Zhou Yu is a meticulous man. If he cannot find the letter at daybreak, he will certainly kill me.” At the fifth watch, Jiang Gan rose and called to Zhou Yu, but Zhou Yu remained asleep. Jiang Gan put on his headcloth and cap, stole quietly out of the tent, summoned his young servant, and went straight out through the camp gate. The soldiers asked, “Where are you going, sir?” Jiang Gan replied, “I fear that my presence here may interfere with the Commander-in-Chief’s affairs, so for now I shall take my leave.” The soldiers did not stop him.

p.src: Jiang Gan boarded his boat and had the oarsmen speed him back to Cao Cao. Cao Cao asked, “Ziyi, how did your mission go?” Jiang Gan replied, “Zhou Yu possesses noble magnanimity and lofty character; mere words cannot sway him.” Cao Cao said angrily, “Not only have you failed again, you have made a laughingstock of yourself!” Jiang Gan said, “Though I could not persuade Zhou Yu, I did learn something for you, Chancellor. Please dismiss those around us.” Jiang Gan produced the letter and related every detail of what had happened to Cao Cao. Cao Cao flew into a rage. “How dare these two villains behave so outrageously!” He immediately summoned Cai Mao and Zhang Yun to his tent. Cao Cao said, “I wish you two to advance the army.” Cai Mao replied, “The troops are not yet fully trained; we must not advance rashly.” Cao Cao shouted angrily, “Once the troops are fully trained, my head will already have been offered to young Zhou!” Cai Mao and Zhang Yun did not understand his meaning and were too terrified to answer. Cao Cao ordered the guards to drag them out and behead them. Presently their heads were offered before the tent, and only then did Cao Cao realize what had happened. “I have fallen into a trap!” he exclaimed. A later poet lamented in verse:
